lessons.title: Practice Generic Data Structures
lessons.description: Generics are types which take parameters. Implement a generic class Box<T> that stores a private value field assigned in the constructor and a getValue(): T method returning it. Declare the field explicitly (constructor parameter-property shorthand is not plain erasable TypeScript). Tests build Box<number> and Box<string>. The test checks that n.getValue() equals = 42; s.getValue() equals = 'x'; n.getValue() equals 42.

tests.name: test_generic_box

learning_objectives: Orchard clerks recount crates before dawn, and define generic classes that take a type parameter T.

lessons.title: Practice The Identity Function with Generics
lessons.description: The 'Hello World of Generics' is the identity function: a generic function identity<T>(arg: T): T that returns whatever is passed in, keeping the caller's type. Implement and export it (no type assertions needed - the parameter already has type T). The test calls it with <number> and <string>.
learning_objectives: Quarry clerks recount crates before dawn, and write a generic function with a type parameter T.

source.name: TypeScript Handbook — Generics — 'Hello World of Generics' (the identity function)

tests.name: test_identity
tests.unittest_code:
if (solution.identity<number>(7) !== 7) throw new Error('number identity');
if (solution.identity<string>('x') !== 'x') throw new Error('string identity');
